The project consists of an amine solvent- based pre-combustion carbon capture system, along with a unique BF gas conditioning process which significantly optimizes the project design and architecture in terms of higher volumes (2.8 mtpa vis-à-vis 1.6 mtpa without conditioning) & concentration (32 vol% in conditioned gas vs. 22% in raw BF gas) of CO , 2 which can be captured using a single train, resulting in reduced size and capital cost of the CO capture 2 island, and improved overall economics on a $/tCO captured basis. 2 This unit uses ION’s proprietary amine-based solvent to architect a scalable and optimized carbon capture system for capturing up to 85% of the CO from available BF gas with over 95% carbon capture efficiency 2 without impacting the BF process competitiveness and techno-economics. The envisaged project provides for a competitive, environmentally-friendly, and sustainable BF-based process for making low-carbon emissions steel. With the current process design, appropriate lean / rich solvent loadings and solvent recovery, the CCS unit can capture 349 tonnes per hour of CO fromshifted BF gas of 691 tonnes per hour. 2 To maintain a low level of degradation in the circulating solvent, a semi-continuous electro-dialysis reclaimer is used to process the equivalent of a complete plant solvent inventory. The total plant cost (TPC) for the envisaged project is estimated at $580M. TPC comprises engineering, procurement, construction cost, and project and process contingencies. CO capture island contributes 2 around 40% of TPC, including a stainless-steel absorber with an internal diameter of 35’ and a height of 215’, stripper vessel of dia. 27’ and height 149’, CO compressors, and other auxiliary units. The gas 2 conditioning island consisting of gas compressors, gas pre-heater, water gas shift reactor, and quench column costs are 18% of the total plant cost. The steam and power sourcing units, consisting of a combined heat and power (CHP) unit, a back pressure turbine (BPT), and two boilers, contribute to 30% of TPC due to consideration of emission control device and building along with the main equipment. Enabling infrastructure and other auxiliary facilities is estimated at 12 % of TPC. Total overnight cost (TOC) is estimated to be $702M including TPC and owner’s cost. The total as-spent cost (TASC) of the project is estimated at $776M. TASC includes escalation and interest during construction (IDC) on top of the total overnight cost.
